results.name: 10 Most Obscure Stephen King Novels, According to Goodreads
results.content:
## 9 'Lisey's Story' (2006)  
### Ratings on Goodreads: 93,932  
One of many Stephen King stories to be about writing, or a writer, in one way or another, **Lisey’s Story** is famously the novel of King’s he’s [singled out as his personal favorite](https://www.syfy.com/syfy-wire/liseys-story-stephen-kings-apple-tv-plot-spoilers-explained). Look, you can see why it means a lot to King personally, since it’s a remarkably personal novel that feels like a love letter to his wife, as well as something that reflects his own thoughts on mortality and legacy, but…  
…like, *Lisey’s Story* is also a bit unreadable. It can be appreciated, and you can understand why King wrote it – and why he likes it – but if you're not Stephen King, or a family member of King’s, **then it’s a bit of a slog to get through. This one is understandably one of his least-read novels**, and it’s hard to recommend it unless you're invested enough in King’s body of work to feel genuinely compelled to read every single thing he’s written.
## 6 'From a Buick 8' (2002)  
### Ratings on Goodreads: 74,391  
**Christine** was the first [Stephen King novel about a spooky car](https://collider.com/christine-movie-john-carpenter/), and then **From a Buick 8** demonstrated that he had more to say with such a premise. Okay, narratively, both books are pretty different, in the sense that *Christine* does actually feel like a whole story (coherent enough, for the most part, in other words), while *From a Buick 8* is chaotic and all over the place in a way that sometimes works, and sometimes proves frustrating.  
At least you don’t feel let down here, the way you might with a good [Stephen King novel that concludes questionably](https://collider.com/stephen-king-endings-most-infamous-ranked/), since the whole of *From a Buick 8* is trippy and confounding. If you like the book, you'll argue that the confounding stuff was all intentional, but **if you're of the view it’s one of King’s weaker ones, you're probably on Team That Should Have Been Clearer**. All these words were regurgitated without describing what happens here, but honestly, what does happen here?
## 1 'Gwendy's Final Task' (2022)  
### Ratings on Goodreads: 22,057  
So, *Never Flinch* is the most recent Stephen King novel, at the time of writing, and that might explain why it has comparatively fewer ratings than most of his works. In five or 10 years, the number of ratings could well have increased quite a bit, but that might not be as likely to happen for **Gwendy’s Final Task**, which is older and has easily the fewest ratings of any novel/stand-alone novella of King’s on Goodreads.  
It's also one of his least essential works, once more co-written with Richard Chizmar, with the most enjoyable parts here just being the references and shout-outs to *The Dark Tower* and its mythos. Otherwise, *Gwendy’s Final Task* is **a bizarre finale that has a now-elderly Gwendy, grappling with dementia, going into space to dispose of the first story’s titular button box**. Yes, really. It’s a novel that answers the question of “Can you still jump the shark if you're countless miles above the ocean?” with a resounding “Yes.”

When it comes to literary universes created in the contemporary era, [Stephen King](https://www.cbr.com/tag/stephen-king/) stands out more than any other author. Known as the **Master of Horror**, he has written dozens of best-selling novels and crafted some of the most memorable literary works in decades.  
Some of Stephen King's most memorable stories have been adapted to film, TV, comics, and other mediums over the years. While these adaptations are not always the best, they do help to communicate to a wider audience just how scary the scariest Stephen King books are.  
*Updated on March 18, 2024, by Andrea Sandoval: Stephen King is known for writing some of the best horror novels in the last four decades. With the new adaptation of 'Salem's Lot finally releasing on Max, we updated this article to further discuss Stephen King's most terrifying novels.*
## 12 Revival Is One of the Most Recent Stephen King's Novels

*Revival* is another overlooked and highly underrated novel by the modern-day Stephen King. The story follows a minister named Charles Jacobs and a man named Jamie Morton. They first met when Jamie was just a child and Charles was a youth minister. Charles became a traveling revival minister and Jamie became a drug addict.  
The entire novel sees these two men spiraling into darkness as they meet each other again a few times over the years. *Revival* explores a new horrifying take on miracle-working ministers by infusing it with a healthy dose of other-dimensional horror. The novel also features one of [the scariest horror movie endings](https://www.cbr.com/great-horror-movies-with-terrible-endings/) that Stephen King has written in years.
## 10 The Stand Is an Eerily Relable Novel  
| Date Published: | October 3, 1978 |
|---|---|
| Publisher: | Doubleday |
| Adaptation: | *The Stand* (2022) miniseries can be streamed on Amazon Prime |

*The Stand* has always been one of Stephen King's most beloved novels and is a favorite among many of his fans. However, the horrors of a flu-like disease known as "Captain Trips" killing almost the entire world's population is scarier than ever given recent world events.  
*The Stand* followed the survivors of the world-decimating plague as outside forces gathered them together. A battle between good and evil introduced one of the scariest villains in Stephen King's literary universe. *The Stand* has had a television adaptation in addition to several films and continues to be one of the most frightening Stephen King books.

results.name: Exploring the Top Five Unsung Stephen King Novels - Wicked Horror
results.content:
In a recent article related to the upcoming release of [Stephen King’s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_King) new novel, *Revival*, apoll asked viewers to rank the top ten best King novels. I was not at all surprised to see that the top three choices were exactly as I predicted – *The Shining, It*, and *The Stand*.  
I’m not suggesting that those books don’t deserve to be on a list depicting the best of King’s work because they do. They are some of his most well-known and loved books that even people who are not fans of his work would recognize. But King has written over fifty novels. And none of the above mentioned choices would even be in my top five – where is the love for the rest of the amazing stories that King has created? So, to remedy that, we have put together a list of the top five unsung Stephen King classics.  
*Needful Things*(Viking, 1991)
*Bag of Bones* (Scribner, 1998)  
This is by far my favorite Stephen King novel. I have read it half a dozen times now, and always tell people that it is a wonderful book to pick up when you just want to read a really, really good story. Bag of Bones deals with an author who returns to his lake to mourn the death of his wife and is confronted by a supernatural presence. It is both a beautiful love story and a beautiful ghost story wrapped up in a mystery that finally concludes with the revelation of a horrifying secret that has plagued the town for a hundred years. By all means, do not judge the quality of the book by the recent television adaptation. Bag of Bones is a mature, heart-breaking, and horrifying novel that will no doubt touch all those who read it.  
*The Dead Zone* (Viking, 1979)
*The Dead Zone* (Viking, 1979)  
Though it spawned a classic film and television series, I still don’t see The Dead Zone get that much recognition as a novel. It is quite possibly King’s most successful novel to date, in that it is extremely successful at achieving what King wanted to do with it. The story’s main character, Johnny Smith, who develops the ability to see into the future after a car accident, is not only the novel’s most important element, but also the best character that King ever created. Smith represents the Everyman, the guy you relate to and can’t help but like from the moment you meet him. The Dead Zone is a fine example of a modern day tragedy, and one that should be on everybody’s reading list, whether you are a King fan or not.

Magnificent, riveting, full of heart, and humor, OTHER WORLDS THAN THESE is a spectacular, propulsive adventure, and features 30 exclusive black and white illustrations by artist Gabriel Rodriguez. OTHER WORLDS THAN THESE will appeal to new King readers and his constant readers.
